source.title: Block Coordinate Descent for Neural Networks Provably Finds Global Minima

record.file_problem: Full paper text supplied; no apparent cutoff or garbling that prevents extraction.
record.tranche_reason: The paper reports its own training results on synthetic regression data, comparing skip connections and singular value bounding (SVB). These are conceptual tests of shortcut and initialization effects, using BCD with gradient updates rather than the benchmark gradient-training recipes in the versions.
record.gate_note: The paper does not report CIFAR or ImageNet results, classification error, random or corrupted labels, SGD or Adam training of the full network, or the two-layer teacher-student experiment. Those version conditions are untested. The cross-entropy classification discussion is a proposed extension, not an experiment. Figure-only trajectories have no precise extracted values.
record.test_reason: The initialization-only SVB ablation directly tests whether conditioning initial weight matrices improves training, bearing on V4 through a different optimizer and regression setting. The shortcut experiments do not test V3's depth-dependent degradation.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is broadly accurate. The authors claim arbitrarily small augmented training objective under their assumptions, including full-row-rank inputs with n ≤ input dimension, suitable initialization and update choices, and activations with a positive derivative lower bound. Their ReLU guarantee uses shortcuts, non-negative projections, and a fixed mixed-sign output layer. Synthetic experiments qualitatively corroborate these guarantees; the ablations show stagnation without SVB and convergence failure without shortcuts.
record.recipe_differences: Uses layer-wise block coordinate descent with auxiliary variables and local gradient updates, rather than the full-network SGD or Adam benchmark recipes in the claim. Synthetic squared-loss regression is tested; classification is discussed only as a possible extension. SVB and a modified ReLU algorithm with skip connections and projections are used.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported outcomes vary with SVB and skip connections. Deeper LeakyReLU networks have slower initial convergence, though loss decreases at all reported depths.

fits_no_version.finding: Modified ReLU BCD decreases loss with shortcuts, whereas the no-shortcut ablation fails to converge.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Identity shortcuts can enable convergence of this auxiliary-variable ReLU BCD procedure on synthetic regression.

fits_no_version.finding: LeakyReLU BCD loss decreases at depths L = 4, 8, 12, with slower initial convergence in deeper networks.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: This BCD procedure remains trainable across the tested fully connected network depths, although initial convergence slows.

record.problems: Experiments use a synthetic regression dataset with n = 500, one teacher network, and five repetitions. The reported results do not test benchmark classification error. Several trajectories are shown in figures without exact numerical values in the text; results for depths L = 8 and L = 12 are only described qualitatively.
record.rows_left_out: No additional results that meet the row criteria were identified. The paper's theoretical convergence bounds and its proposed classification extension are not empirical training outcomes for the claim's benchmark classification versions.

untested.parts: CIFAR classification error, corrupted or random labels, convolutional networks trained with SGD or Adam, and size or regularization comparisons.
Two-layer ReLU teacher-student local-minimum frequencies and the benefit of one or two extra student neurons.
Depth-dependent training-error degradation and its prevention by identity shortcuts in the named convolutional settings; very deep tanh and Fixup exceptions.

Activation matching, signal and gradient propagation across layers, increased trainable depth attributable to initialization, orthogonal versus Gaussian initialization, and very deep tanh or convolutional networks.
Learning-rate stability thresholds, catapult recovery, curvature or sharpness trajectories, and divergence relative to those thresholds.
Batch-normalization comparisons, accuracy gains per training time, higher learning-rate tolerance, and Fixup comparisons.

record.verdict_notes: V4 support concerns the measured initialization benefit only; the experiment does not verify the full propagation mechanism or depth claims. No verdict follows from the paper's proposed classification extension or its general convergence guarantees alone.

versions.untested_parts: CIFAR-10/CIFAR-100 classification error; SGD or Adam training from random initialization; corrupted or random labels; model size and training duration comparisons.
Two-layer ReLU teacher-student problems; spurious local minima; student-to-teacher width comparisons.

Batch-normalized convolutional networks on ImageNet or CIFAR-10, depth comparisons, longer training comparisons, and Fixup or other normalization-free residual recipes. The paper compares a ReLU network with and without skip connections only on synthetic regression data using BCD.

Activation-matched initializations, signal or gradient propagation, orthogonal versus Gaussian weights, tanh networks, and very deep convolutional networks. The paper tests SVB at initialization versus omitting it in a four-hidden-layer LeakyReLU synthetic-regression experiment.
Learning rates above a stability threshold, loss increases and curvature or sharpness changes, and divergence.
Batch normalization comparisons, learning-rate tolerance, accuracy curves on MNIST/CIFAR-10/ImageNet, and normalization-free Fixup comparisons.

rows.note: The compared algorithm also uses non-negative projection; the reported comparison isolates the presence of skip connections at the stated recipe level, not shortcut effects independently of other design choices.

rows.check: Failure without shortcuts at one depth does not establish V3's depth-degradation effect. Even if linked, this failure would be consistent with shortcut benefits, not a reversed effect or a challenge.
